claims.text: Increasing vacancy concentration in HfNbTaTiZr enhances diffusion-assisted dislocation climb at elevated temperatures.
Increasing vacancy concentration in HfNbTaTiZr alters vibrational entropy.
Higher vacancy concentration lowers the elevated-temperature yield stress of HfNbTaTiZr.
Higher vacancy concentration increases the strain-rate sensitivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
Higher vacancy concentration modifies the thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Higher vacancy concentration modifies the elastic moduli of HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast or minimally processed HfNbTaTiZr has a low, naturally occurring vacancy concentration suitable as a baseline.
Controlled cold work followed by tailored annealing can produce HfNbTaTiZr samples with systematically varied vacancy densities.
Elevated vacancy concentrations enhance diffusion pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Elevated vacancy concentrations modify phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Vacancy-induced changes in phonon scattering and vibrational entropy adjust the balance between thermal expansion and elastic stiffness.
The predicted mechanical, thermal-expansion, and elastic-property changes should correlate with measured vacancy density.
The proposed vacancy-mediated relationships apply between 300°C and 1100°C.
Outside 300°C to 1100°C, other microstructural or thermal phenomena may predominate.
